title: Paper Trading and Live Portfolio Monitoring Now Available in Claude with Alpaca
summary: Discover the Alpaca Claude Connectors. Monitor live portfolios, execute paper trades, and analyze market trends using natural language in Claude.
body_markdown:
We’re excited to share that you can now use your Alpaca account for paper trading and live portfolio monitoring in Claude. This builds on Alpaca’s agentic tooling initiatives, including[Alpaca’s MCP Server](https://alpaca.markets/mcp-server?ref=alpaca.markets) ,[CLI](https://alpaca.markets/blog/alpaca-introduces-cli-for-trading-api/) , and other AI connectors.


The[Alpaca Paper Trading connector](https://claude.ai/directory/alpaca-paper-trading?ref=alpaca.markets) provides access to paper trading through[Alpaca's Trading API](https://alpaca.markets/algotrading?ref=alpaca.markets) and[Market Data](https://alpaca.markets/data?ref=alpaca.markets) , enabling you to analyze market trends, monitor your account, and place simulated trades across stocks, ETFs, and options using natural language. The[Alpaca Live connector](https://claude.ai/directory/alpaca-live-mcp?ref=alpaca.markets) provides access to your live account through Alpaca's Trading API and Market Data API for portfolio monitoring and market research.


*AI-generated responses may contain errors, omissions, or inaccuracies and should be independently verified before being relied upon for investment decisions or trading activity.*

Paper trading uses simulated funds with no real capital. The walkthrough below helps you practice the account-and-order workflow; it does not establish how a strategy would perform with real money.


## **Using the Alpaca Paper Trading Connector**


### **Start with an account check**


[Connect to the Alpaca Paper Trading connector in Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/alpaca-paper-trading?ref=alpaca.markets) and complete the Alpaca sign-in and authorization flow. To follow along with the prompts below, you need an Alpaca paper account.[Create an account](https://app.alpaca.markets/signup?ref=alpaca.markets) if you don't already have one.


Before authorizing the connection, review the requested account permissions and ensure that you are connecting the intended paper trading account.


Your first prompt can be:


```text
Show my Alpaca paper account balance, buying power, and account status.
```


**Illustrative paper trading account. All balances, positions, and results shown are simulated and do not represent actual trading performance.**


Compare the response with the paper account in your Alpaca dashboard. Buying power tells you what the account can use for orders under its current limits.


If the account or balances do not match, resolve the connection before proceeding. If you have multiple paper accounts, confirm which account you have connected. Do not use an order to test an unresolved account mismatch.


### **Submit a paper order, then check its status**


Once you have verified the account, try submitting a simulated order. Replace the “AAPL” placeholder with the symbol of a stock or ETF supported by your paper account.


*The following example demonstrates simulated order submission only and does not involve purchasing securities in the actual market. Review all AI-generated order details before submission.*


```text
In my Alpaca paper account, submit a day market order to buy 1 share
of AAPL. Show the order ID and current status returned by Alpaca.
```


Read the response before taking another action. An order acknowledgment does not establish that the order has been filled.


Then ask:


```text
Retrieve the current status of that paper order.
Show the filled quantity and average fill price if available,
then refresh my paper positions and buying power.
```


**Simulated order execution. Paper trading fills may differ materially from actual market executions.**


The distinction matters when an order remains open, fills partially, or is rejected. Inspect the returned status and any rejection message instead of assuming that a conversational confirmation means the position changed.


*Users should independently verify order statuses, account balances, and positions through their Alpaca account rather than relying solely on AI-generated confirmations.*


## **Using the Alpaca Live Connector**


[Connect the Alpaca Live connector in Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/alpaca-live-mcp?ref=alpaca.markets) and complete the Alpaca sign-in and authorization flow for your live account. Learn more about how to open a live account as a[non-US resident](https://alpaca.markets/learn/live-trading-account-non-us?ref=alpaca.markets) or as a[US resident](https://alpaca.markets/learn/live-trading-account-us-resident?ref=alpaca.markets)[.](https://alpaca.markets/disclosures?ref=alpaca.markets)


Start by checking your balances and positions:


```text
Summarize my live Alpaca account balances, buying power, and open positions.
Include the retrieval time and identify any information you could not retrieve.
```


**Illustrative account information is provided for demonstration purposes only. Securities shown do not constitute investment recommendations. Account information may be incomplete, delayed, or inaccurate and should be verified against the applicable Alpaca account.**


A follow-up can narrow the view:


```text
Show my open orders and recent fills.
```


**Note:** The Alpaca Live connector does not place orders. You must use Alpaca's Trading API or Dashboard for live execution. Live trading involves financial risk, including the potential loss of principal.


## **Know what the connection can return**


Account access, market data access, and order execution are separate checks. A successful balance request does not establish that every symbol, data feed, or asset class is available.


The market data Claude can retrieve depends on the subscription associated with your authenticated Alpaca account. Free and paid plans differ in feed coverage, data recency, and request limits. Check your Alpaca account's subscription and the[Market Data API documentation](https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/about-market-data-api?ref=alpaca.markets) to confirm what is included.


If a market-data request fails, inspect the returned message and your Alpaca account's data access before changing the prompt. Options data will only appear for accounts with those asset classes enabled. Check eligibility and enablement in your Alpaca account, and confirm that the requested action is supported by the connector. Reconnecting alone may not resolve a missing permission or unsupported tool.


Simulation has its own limits. Alpaca's[paper trading documentation](https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/paper-trading?ref=alpaca.markets) lists factors the simulation does not model, including market impact, price slippage due to latency, order queue position, and regulatory fees. A completed paper order demonstrates the simulated workflow. It does not predict a live fill.


## **Where to go next**


To try paper trading in Claude, connect the[Alpaca Paper Trading Connector](https://claude.ai/directory/alpaca-paper-trading?ref=alpaca.markets) . Check your account, place a simulated test order, and check its status until it's complete. You can then review the order details in your Alpaca account alongside the conversation.


To monitor your live portfolio, connect the[Alpaca Live Connector](https://claude.ai/directory/alpaca-live-mcp?ref=alpaca.markets) .


For more on paper trading, live accounts, and building with Alpaca's Trading API, see the related resources below.
